# 🤝 Contributing to FewMath

Welcome! 🎉 We’re excited that you want to contribute to FewMath — a cross-language, high-performance mathematical library.

Whether you're fixing bugs, improving documentation, optimizing algorithms, or adding new features, your contribution is appreciated! ❤️

## 🚀 How to Contribute

### Fork the Repository
Click the Fork button at the top-right corner of this repository and clone it to your local machine:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-username/FewMath.git
```

### Create a New Branch
Always create a new branch for your work:
```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
```

### Make Your Changes
- Write clean, efficient, and well-documented code.
- Follow existing code style and folder structure.
- Add meaningful comments where required.

### Add Tests (If Applicable)
If you're adding a new feature or algorithm, kindly write tests for it under the `tests/` directory.

### Commit and Push
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Add: Your meaningful commit message"
git push origin feature/your-feature-name
```

### Create a Pull Request
Once you're ready, create a Pull Request from your branch to the main branch and describe your changes clearly.

## 📄 Contribution Guidelines
- Follow the MIT License terms.
- Make sure your code compiles and passes all tests.
- Use clear and descriptive commit messages.
- Keep pull requests small and focused on a single feature/fix.
- Be respectful in discussions and reviews.

## 📌 FewMath Development Phases
You can contribute in any of the following phases:
- Algebra Module (GCD, LCM, Modular Arithmetic, etc.)
- Number Theory (Prime Factorization, Sieve Algorithms, etc.)
- Statistics & Calculus (Mean, Median, Mode, Integration, etc.)
- Performance Benchmarking
- Documentation Improvement

## 🙌 Need Help?
If you’re new to open source or need help setting up the project, feel free to create an Issue or reach out to the maintainers.

Happy Contributing! 🚀
